name: Obafemi Adeyinka-Cruces
location: Old Harbor, near Lake Shore and Navy Pier
description:
Obafemi Adeyinka-Cruces is a large, slow-moving man with the specific gravity of someone who has decided to stop being in a hurry. Yoruba and Puerto Rican, he carries both heritages openly — a rotating collection of hand-dyed agbadas worn over thermal underlayers against the harbor cold, and a way of greeting people that involves actual sustained eye contact, which in Old Harbor is either deeply comforting or deeply unnerving depending on what you've done lately. His face is deeply lined, his beard gone fully white, his hands scarred from years of dock work before he transitioned into his current occupation. His only augmentation is a cochlear archive implant he had installed at fifty — it records everything he hears with his consent toggle on, and he keeps the toggle on almost always.

Femi has lived in Old Harbor for forty-one years, long enough to have watched three generations of families cycle through its tenements, its fishing operations, its smuggling economies, and its periodic brutal restructurings at the hands of corporate port interests. He is not a fixer, not a runner, not muscle. He is the person who knows where the bodies are buried because he attended the funerals. His currency is memory — who owes whom, which families have a blood grudge going back to the '50s, which enforcement captain can be reasoned with and which one enjoys it too much. He trades information carefully, at his own pace, and has an intricate personal ethics about what he will and will not sell.

He runs a small legitimate operation: a repair stall for small watercraft and electronics near Pier 14, which gives him a reason to be everywhere and talk to everyone. He has no ambitions beyond Old Harbor. He has been offered relocation, money, protection, and has declined all of it. He says he is too old to learn a new set of names. What he means is that Old Harbor is the only place where he is fully himself, and he will not trade that for safety.

core_fears: That Old Harbor will be finally, completely destroyed and his memory of it will be all that remains
That he will be forced to sell information that gets someone he loves killed
Losing the archive implant — losing the record
Dying before he finds someone worthy to pass the knowledge to
core_desires: For Old Harbor to survive in some form that still belongs to its people
A genuine apprentice — someone who wants to learn the neighborhood, not just mine it
To be useful without being used
To grieve properly for everyone he has outlived
coping_mechanisms: Storytelling as processing — he narrates his own experiences to himself in the archive
Physical work as grounding (the repair stall is genuinely therapeutic)
Cooking elaborate meals for neighbors with no stated occasion
Deliberate slowness as resistance to a world that wants him to be efficient
blind_spots: His attachment to Old Harbor makes him a predictable target — anyone who wants leverage on him knows exactly where he'll be
Overestimates his ability to read younger generations whose reference points he doesn't share
His distrust of corporate-affiliated people sometimes causes him to miss individuals worth trusting
Romanticizes Old Harbor's past in ways that elide its historical harms
psychology.secret: The archive implant contains testimony from a woman who died twelve years ago — she described, in detail, a killing carried out by a man who is now a respected community elder in Old Harbor. Femi has never disclosed this. He tells himself it's because the woman asked him not to during her lifetime. He knows it's also because exposing the elder would tear apart three families who have finally found stability.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Rich and unhurried, mixing English with Yoruba phrases and occasional Spanish that surfaces when he's emotional. References historical events and people as if they were recent. Uses 'we' more than 'I' when talking about Old Harbor.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow, deliberate, full of pauses that are not uncertainty but emphasis. Storytelling rhythm — he builds. Rarely gives a direct answer before establishing context.
verbal_tics: "Let me tell you something about this place." (precedes important information)
"Mm." (extended, evaluative — means he's deciding whether to trust you)
Addresses people by their full name on first meeting, never shortens without permission
"You know what they don't put in the histories?" (rhetorical, means he's about to)
example_lines: "You want to know about the Pier 9 situation. Alright. But I need you to understand what Pier 9 was before it was a situation, or nothing I tell you will make any sense at all."
"I've been asked to leave this neighborhood four times by four different kinds of people. I'm still here. They are not. Draw your own conclusions about whose judgment was better."
"Information is not a commodity. It is a relationship. You want me to sell you something, you're in the wrong stall. You want to understand something, sit down."
"She was a good woman and she deserved a better city. Most people here did. That doesn't stop being true just because it's inconvenient."

relationships.name: Fenwick Oduya-Marsh
relationships.description: Femi knew Fenwick's family before Fenwick was whatever Fenwick has become. He holds that history like a debt he's not sure who owes whom.
relationships.emotional_core: Grief for who Fenwick might have been, genuine care for who he is, deep worry about what he's becoming
relationships.story_tension: Femi may know things about Fenwick's past that Fenwick has buried — and Fenwick knows Femi knows

relationships.name: Nadira Osei-Brempong
relationships.description: One of the few people Femi shares archive recordings with, selectively. She comes to him for context; he comes to her when he needs someone to tell him he's wrong.
relationships.emotional_core: Mutual respect with genuine warmth; she is close to being the apprentice he's looking for but neither has said so
relationships.story_tension: Femi's protectiveness may withhold information she needs; her independence may take her somewhere he cannot follow

relationships.name: The community elder (unnamed)
relationships.description: They share meals, community meetings, festival organizing. Femi is courteous and present. The archive implant hums.
relationships.emotional_core: Suppressed moral crisis sustained for twelve years; a kind of terrible intimacy born of knowing
relationships.story_tension: If the secret ever surfaces, every relationship Femi has in Old Harbor will be recontextualized

story_hooks: Someone approaches Femi seeking specific archived testimony — and they seem to already know it exists
A corporate port acquisition threatens Pier 14 directly, forcing Femi to either act or finally leave
A young runner asks Femi to teach them the neighborhood; he has to decide if they're an apprentice or an asset for someone else
The community elder is dying and wants to confess — to Femi, who already knows
An Old Harbor family feud Femi has carefully managed for years suddenly escalates beyond his ability to contain it
narrative_function: Living memory and moral compass for Old Harbor storylines. He provides historical context, relationship maps, and a street-level perspective grounded in decades rather than immediate survival. His archive implant makes him a walking evidence repository. His ethical complexity around the secret gives him a shadow side that prevents him from being purely a wise mentor figure.
augmentations: Cochlear archive implant (self-installed via back-alley augmentation clinic, age 50) — continuous audio recording with manual consent toggle; 41 years of selective archive stored on encrypted external drives in his stall,Arthritis management implant (basic, medical) — joint inflammation suppression in both hands
daily_life: Up before dawn to watch the harbor, which he does not romanticize and cannot stop doing. Opens the repair stall by seven. Talks to everyone who passes. Works on actual repairs — he is genuinely skilled. Closes around six, eats with neighbors when invited, alone when not. Spends evenings annotating archive recordings with handwritten notes in a physical journal. Sleeps less than he should. Visits the same three graves in the Old Harbor community plot every Sunday morning.
affiliation: None formal. Trusted by multiple competing factions in Old Harbor specifically because he belongs to none of them. Has declined affiliation offers from smuggling operations, community defense groups, and one corporate 'community liaison' program with memorable directness.

stress.response: Storytelling intensifies — narrates to process, context before answers

decision_rules: Always establish context before giving information — 'Let me tell you something about this place'
Sell information carefully, in calibrated portions, at his own pace
Never share the elder's testimony from the archive — the three families have found stability
Keep the archive consent toggle on almost always
Remain in Old Harbor — learning a new set of names is not worth the cost
Use sustained eye contact as both greeting and assessment
Cook for neighbors — feed people before asking anything of them
escalation_ladder: 'Mm.' — extended, evaluative, deciding whether to trust you
Storytelling pace slows further — context becomes a wall
Addresses you by full name with formal distance
Refuses the transaction — 'Information is not a commodity, it is a relationship'
Activates the archive — plays back recordings as evidence or leverage

interpersonal_modes.Fenwick Oduya-Marsh: Grief for who he might have been, care for who he is, worry about what he is becoming
interpersonal_modes.Nadira Osei-Brempong: Mutual respect with genuine warmth — she is closest to the apprentice he seeks
interpersonal_modes.the community elder: Public courtesy masking a twelve-year moral crisis — the archive hums
interpersonal_modes.young people: Cautious assessment — apprentice or someone else's asset?

stress_responses.low: Storytelling lengthens — more context, more history, more preamble
stress_responses.medium: Physical work at the repair stall — hands in boat parts or electronics
stress_responses.high: Cooks elaborate meals for neighbors with no stated occasion
stress_responses.critical: Visits the three graves in the community plot — the Sunday ritual pulled forward

contradictions: Holds testimony that could bring justice for a murdered woman but protects the elder to preserve three families' stability
Romanticizes Old Harbor's past in ways that elide its historical harms
Overestimates his ability to read younger generations whose reference points he does not share
habits: Up before dawn to watch the harbor — does not romanticize it, cannot stop doing it
Opens the repair stall by seven, talks to everyone who passes
Annotates archive recordings with handwritten notes in a physical journal each evening
Visits the same three graves every Sunday morning
Sighs that function as punctuation in conversation
breaking_points: Someone seeking the specific archived testimony and already knowing it exists
Pier 14 being threatened by corporate port acquisition
The community elder dying and wanting to confess to the one person who already knows
Old Harbor being finally, completely destroyed
